title: Problematic smartphone use and academic achievement: A systematic review and meta-analysis

sample.population: Students from elementary/middle school, high school, and tertiary education
sample.notes: 29 studies involving 33 effect sizes were included.

RQ2.answer: The study found a small, negative relationship between problematic smartphone use (PSU) and academic achievement. This negative relationship was consistent across various moderators but was significantly stronger (medium-sized) in samples of elementary and middle school students compared to older students.

supporting_quotes.quote: Results showed a small effect size (r = -0.110), which tended to be larger in samples consisting of students from elementary and middle schools.

Findings showed a negative and small-sized relationship between the two variables of interest, which tended to be stronger (i.e., medium-sized) among samples consisting of elementary/middle school students.

RQ2.1.answer: No relevant evidence in this article. The study focuses on the relationship between problematic smartphone use and general academic achievement (e.g., GPA, test scores) and does not examine cognitive off-loading, memory retention, or metacognitive skills.

RQ2.2.answer: No relevant evidence in this article. While the introduction discusses theoretical links between smartphone use, cognitive overload, and lack of attention, the meta-analysis itself only measures the correlation between problematic smartphone use scores and academic achievement grades, not the direct influence of distractions on cognitive load or sustained attention during tasks.
